Well, the previous sticky has been up for a few days and I think it has garnered all the responses and suggestions it was going to, so now we move on to the next stage.

Going over the top comments I have decided that the most prudent course of action would be to, as @CujoQuarrel suggested, hunt down the trolls and eat their livers.

However, upon further reflection, it was brought to my attention that cannibalism might actually be against the law in some countries, so instead I have decided to do as @peaceseeker suggested and implement some Guidelines.

These will not be subverse rules, punishable by submission deletions or banning if broken, but rather will serve to establish expectations of what the Users of /v/Linux like and expect to see in /v/Linux.

The only exception to this will be spam posts, the definition of which I think will need to be broadened to include heavy submission brigading from other subverses. After all, I can think of few other acts that better fit the criteria required to be considered spamming.

In addition I hope it will provide some guidance for anyone wanting to submit content and help them avoid being heavily downvoated by unintentionally submitting something that will likely not be well received, or better suited for another subverse. Submitters will of course still be free to submit something that doesn't fall within the guidelines, but I don't want to hear cries of downvoat bots or brigading, should they find such posts going into the negative.

Now, I have some ideas about what should and should not be in these Guidelines, and if I were an asshole I could implement them without asking anyone's opinion on the matter. Thankfully, despite what you may have heard, or experienced first hand, I am not as much of an asshole as that, so, this sticky will be used to gather suggestions for what should be in those Guidelines.

Just to be clear, I am only looking for suggestions of what you think should be welcomed in /v/Linux, not what you think should not be. Once these guidelines are implemented, anything that is to be posted that is not covered by them should be assumed as potentially a risky click for the submitter's SCP. Might be welcomed, might not be. Their choice to roll the dice and see.

So, let us discuss.
